opening.argument: The meeting ties earning potential to recruitment and progressively expensive activation. Leaders are told “we need to invite people every day,” while the speaker defines an upgrade as “the activation of the next, more expensive level” and links pushing participants to higher levels with “more income.” The structure routes rewards through activated hierarchy: “The reward for the upgrade goes to your upline partner provided that they already have this level activated and so on.” It also warns that activating only two or three levels may leave a participant disappointed if someone from the team overtakes them. These are strong indicators of recruitment commissions and tiered matrices, though the record does not establish completed payments, actual losses, or independently verified reward outcomes.
